requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct an agent that cannot ask the user in the session to stop, leaving the drafts uncommitted, and report the revised drafts and the design questions.
rationale:
**Obligation.** The requirement has one obligation. The `habeas-requirements` skill must direct an agent that cannot ask the user in the session to do three things: stop, leave the drafts uncommitted, and report the revised drafts and the design questions. The requirement is about the text of a skill asset, so a text-presence test is the appropriate way to check it.

**Test.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_stops_and_reports_when_it_cannot_ask_the_user]` carries `{test}` for this requirement. It calls `assert_phrases("habeas-requirements", ...)` with the phrase "If you cannot ask the user in this session, stop, leave the drafts uncommitted, and report them with the design questions".

**Assertion.** `assert_phrases` passes the bundled skill text to `assert_text`. `assert_text` asserts `text.contains(phrase)` and panics if the phrase is missing. I did not read `bundled_skill`. I took the whitespace collapsing from the evidence rationale, not from the source. It matters because the skill's line wraps would otherwise break the match.

**Mapping.**
- The condition, an agent that cannot ask the user, is covered by the phrase "cannot ask the user in this session".
- Stop is covered by "stop".
- Leaving the drafts uncommitted is covered by "leave the drafts uncommitted".
- Reporting the drafts and the design questions is covered by "report them with the design questions". "Them" refers to the drafts. The skill text, found in the Workflow section of `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, uses the same wording.

The test would fail if any directive were dropped or reworded, so it enforces all three. The text names no other boundaries or modes. I found no gap.
